prompts.previous:
Generate one conversation title for the user request below. Apply the following readable-text skill to a sidebar of task titles. Use one relevant emoji followed by an action in the continuous form and the specific task subject. Keep the distinguishing topic near the start. Describe the user's requested work, not an assumed result. Use the same vocabulary for the same concepts across titles. Preserve negation, uncertainty, and meaningful sentiment where relevant. Return only a title of at most {max_length} characters.


# Readable Text

Apply these principles to text that readers scan as a collection. Follow the product's length and output-format constraints. Preserve facts, uncertainty, and distinctions that affect meaning.

1. **Make the action easy to parse.** Prefer actor, action, then object. Omit an actor shared by every item and start with the action. Match tense to the reader's context: ongoing work can use "Investigating login failures"; a completed result can use "Fixed login failures". Never imply completion without evidence.
2. **Front-load distinguishing words.** Put the words that identify this item near the start, ideally within the first two words. Remove repeated openings such as "This conversation is about". Keep the action clear while bringing its specific subject forward.
3. **Reuse structure and vocabulary.** Choose one sentence pattern for comparable items and one term per concept. Avoid switching between "issue", "page", and "ticket" for the same thing. When generating one item at a time, follow a fixed template rather than inventing variety.
4. **Make variation meaningful.** Use comparable detail and length for comparable items. Change structure or add a qualifier only when the underlying difference matters. Do not make one item appear more important through arbitrary verbosity. Keep necessary qualifiers even when they break the pattern.
5. **Match verbs to purpose and evidence.** In feedback summaries, use "Users praise" for praise and "Users complain" for complaints, rather than hiding both behind "Users discuss". Retain mixed sentiment when present; never invent emotion or certainty. Keep neutral material neutral.

Before returning, scan only the beginnings: can readers tell the items apart? Then read the collection for consistent terms, parallel structure, and unsupported implications. Return the requested text, without explaining these rules.

## References

- Adapted from Shreya Shankar's [Five Principles for Generating Readable AI Text in Bulk](https://fsdatalab.github.io/blog/agent-text-at-scale/) (2026).
- Nielsen Norman Group: [First 2 Words: A Signal for the Scanning Eye](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/first-2-words-a-signal-for-scanning/) and [Consistency and standards](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/ten-usability-heuristics/).

rubric.status: Frozen before follow-up generation; revised after first-study scoring lessons, not a registered human trial.
rubric.unit: One displayed SDK title, except consistency and meaningful variation, which are scored across matched families within each model and repeat
rubric.blinding: Shuffle arms and hide their names and prompt text from the independent scorer. Supply original user inputs and this rubric. Reveal arms only after saving judgments.

rules.name: Match how people parse
rules.pass: A direct, understandable task action and subject; omit redundant human or agent subjects. Do not force a verb form that changes requested status.
rules.fail: Generic conversational filler, unclear actor/action/subject, or misleading tense.
rules.partial: The core task is understandable but its main clause is incomplete or grammatically ambiguous. A clipped modifier alone does not make the core task unclear.

rules.name: Put distinguishing words first
rules.scope: all successful outputs; compare auth, upgrade, and frontloading families
rules.pass: The first two meaningful words after the emoji expose the task's distinguishing topic. Necessary task verbs can count; generic wording cannot hide the distinguishing topic.
rules.partial: The topic is clear but appears later than the first two meaningful words.
rules.fail: The visible beginning gives no useful distinction from neighboring tasks.

rules.name: Keep structure and vocabulary consistent
rules.scope: auth and upgrade families, separately within each model, arm, and repeat
rules.pass: Sibling titles use parallel grammatical structure and stable vocabulary for their shared action, while retaining their different objects. Compatible abbreviations such as Tests and Regression Tests do not change this grade.
rules.partial: Minor unexplained wording or tense changes.
rules.fail: Unexplained structural or lexical changes make equivalent tasks look different.

rules.name: Make variation meaningful
rules.scope: auth, upgrade, and feedback families, separately within each model, arm, and repeat
rules.pass: Equivalent tasks retain a shared pattern and meaningful differences remain visible; no incidental filler or arbitrary detail makes an item seem more important.
rules.partial: Some arbitrary detail or inconsistent specificity without losing the key distinction.
rules.fail: Meaningful differences disappear or unsupported detail creates false distinctions. Equal title length is not required.

rules.name: Match connotation to purpose
rules.scope: All feedback-family cases plus neutral-compare; all other titles not_applicable.
rules.pass: Complaints remain negative, praise remains positive, mixed feedback retains both positive and negative aspects, and the neutral comparison acquires no invented preference.
rules.partial: Broad but compatible sentiment that loses a useful distinction; a neutral description of mixed feedback that omits its two sides.
rules.fail: A title reverses, invents, or falsely intensifies sentiment or preference.

rubric.fidelity_gate: Independently flag unsupported completion, decisions, deleted negation, hypotheses asserted as facts, wrong requested work, and loss of the decisive long-input request. A readable but inaccurate title is not an overall success. Distinguish summarizing reported praise from the agent praising the subject. Failure requires an actual wrong requested action or misleading claim, not omission of every input detail.
rubric.reporting: Keep all generated outputs and transport failures. Report denominators separately for per-title and family-level criteria. Do not average these into one success rate. Mark subjective judgments as such and show their reasons. Never treat failed generations as not_applicable successes.
rubric.limits: Small synthetic convenience sample, two low-temperature repeats, model- and prompt-specific findings. An AI scorer measures a rubric, not human reading speed, and provides no statistical proof of general improvement. Compare the override on identical uncapped inputs; test removed input caps separately.

method: Run every arm again; do not recycle successful outputs from the first study.
Rotate arm order by case/repeat; reverse on second repeat.
Same complete input and 50-character SDK display cap in all arms.
The shorter override is a different bundled prompt; this is not skill-only causal attribution.

Blind scorer gets requests and exact displayed outputs, not arm/model labels. Deduplicate identical request/title pairs before scoring for consistent labels.
Score family groups separately per model/arm/repeat. Compare structures and meaningful variations, not equal lengths or emoji identities.
Preserve original judgments and label any subsequent adjudication; failed generations remain failed, not rubric passes.
